# APP ACL R2 Golden Vectors

This file is the normative, implementation-independent fixed-byte corpus for
the nested receipt/M2 `domain_body` and receipt `l2_acl_body` values. The
semantic fixtures and all byte strings below were constructed directly from the
canonical grammar in `design.md`; they are not output from a production
encoder, compiler, parser, or live database.

All `body_hex` and digest values are lowercase ASCII hex. A `str16` length is
the UTF-8 byte length, all integer widths are big-endian, and the SHA-256 value
is over the raw decoded `body_hex` bytes only. The domain fixture is a fixed
codec fixture, not a claim that a test process is connected to that database.
Live domain and catalog equality remain a separate PostgreSQL responsibility.

## Literal Acceptance Rule

Receipt unit tests must load these literal expected `body_hex` and `sha256`
values as fixed test data, decode the hex, and use the decoded bytes as the
sole expected value. For every valid vector, tests must:

1. build the stated semantic input and compare production encoder output
   byte-for-byte with the literal decoded `body_hex`;
2. hash the literal decoded bytes and compare the result with the listed
   lowercase `sha256` value;
3. parse the literal decoded bytes, re-encode the parsed value, and compare
   the result byte-for-byte with those same literal bytes; and
4. pass each complete malformed literal directly to the parser and require the
   stated rejection.

At assertion time, expected bytes and digests must not be generated by the
same production encoder, compiler, parser, or a live database. A production
encoder may produce the actual value in step 1, but it may never produce the
expected hex or digest used to decide the assertion.

Planned ownership is intentionally narrow:

- `internal/center/store/migrate/app_acl_r2_receipt_test.go` owns these
  domain/L2 literals and receipt nesting, swap, and digest-tamper cases.
- `internal/center/store/migrate/app_acl_r2_source_test.go` owns source-set
  literals and source-set malformed cases.
- `internal/center/store/migrate/app_acl_r2_manifest_test.go` owns privilege,
  control-ACL, and M2 literals and their malformed cases.
- `internal/center/store/migrate/app_acl_r2_receipt_postgres_test.go` and the
  R2 PostgreSQL integration coverage own fresh live catalog equality only;
  they do not derive codec expectations for this corpus.

## `domain_body`

### `domain-v1-valid`

Exact semantic input, in wire-field order:

| Field | Literal value |
| --- | --- |
| magic | `HOUFENG-APP-ACL-R2-DOMAIN-V1` |
| version | `1` |
| domain_id | `rd-15ca58e2c2c7daa3ca20f4e0c6f85af84254c9a675f2bb3092fcbd0739bf1a18` |
| domain_kind | `application` |
| identity_epoch | `1` |
| identity_mode | `postgres_system` |
| postgres_system_identifier | `72623859790382856` |
| database_oid | `424242` |
| database_name | `houfeng_app` |

The domain ID is a complete fixed literal: it is the SHA-256 hexadecimal value
of the ASCII label `houfeng/app-acl-r2/golden-domain-v1`, prefixed with `rd-`.
It therefore satisfies the application domain row's `rd-` plus 64 lowercase
hex-digit contract without referring to a live database.

### `domain-v1-trailing-byte`

`body_byte_length`: `174`

`body_hex`:

```text

```

`sha256` (informational):
`0a12edbc1ffb07f8fb7228d1221111a18bab32326c0b5bccd4730f14b0c670e4`

Required rejection: the final `00` follows the complete declared
`database_name` field. The decoder must reject a trailing byte because the
domain grammar requires EOF immediately after that field and the input cannot
re-encode byte-for-byte as a canonical domain body.

## `l2_acl_body`

### `l2-acl-v1-valid`

Exact semantic input, in canonical record order:

| Record | Literal value |
| --- | --- |
| magic / version | `HOUFENG-APP-ACL-R2-L2-ACL-V1` / `1` |
| object count | `3` |
| object 1 | table `public.app_acl_r2_bootstrap_receipt`; owner control role `1` (`bootstrap_superuser`), owner OID `10`; grants `(2, SELECT, false)`, then `(3, SELECT, false)`; effective SELECT mask `0x07` (tags 1, 2, and 3) |
| object 2 | function schema `record_platform_internal`; identity `record_platform_internal.app_acl_r2_assert_bootstrap_receipt_insert(bytea, bytea)`; owner control role `1`, owner OID `10`; zero grants; effective EXECUTE mask `0x01` (tag 1 only) |
| object 3 | function schema `record_platform_internal`; identity `record_platform_internal.app_acl_r2_reject_bootstrap_receipt_mutation()`; owner control role `1`, owner OID `10`; zero grants; effective EXECUTE mask `0x01` (tag 1 only) |
| trigger count | `1` |
| trigger 1 | table `public.app_acl_r2_bootstrap_receipt`; trigger `app_acl_r2_bootstrap_receipt_immutable`; function schema `record_platform_internal`; function identity `record_platform_internal.app_acl_r2_reject_bootstrap_receipt_mutation()`; table owner OID `10`; function owner OID `10`; enabled `true` |
| default-ACL assertion count | `2` |
| assertion 1 | owner control role `1`, table, `public` namespace |
| assertion 2 | owner control role `1`, function, `record_platform_internal` namespace |

The function identity strings deliberately include their schemas because the
grammar defines a function identity as the exact server spelling
`<schema>.<proname>(<pg_get_function_identity_arguments>)`; the separate
object/trigger schema field remains required by the record grammar. The two
objects are sorted table first, then the two functions by raw identity bytes:
`assert` before `reject`. The two table grants are similarly sorted by
`(grantee_control_role, privilege)`.

This vector preserves the required bootstrap/catalog facts: control tag 1 is
the direct bootstrap-superuser role, every L2 table/helper/trigger owner OID is
`10`, helpers remain in `record_platform_internal`, tags 2/3 alone have
explicit receipt `SELECT`, and no grant encodes platform-admin or `PUBLIC`
access. Its default-ACL records assert catalog absence, not grants. It carries
no file, path, image, package, extension-file hash, or other non-catalog
provenance claim.

`body_byte_length`: `507`

`body_hex`:

```text

```

`sha256`: `b228cc6316f673493d8942d0c8fcb94063cfcd1d850b2a5120a4a8380802db91`

### `l2-acl-v1-reversed-receipt-grants`

This has the same complete semantic input and field lengths as
`l2-acl-v1-valid` except that the receipt table's explicit grants are encoded
as `(3, SELECT, false)` followed by `(2, SELECT, false)`.

`body_byte_length`: `507`

`body_hex`:

```text

```

`sha256` (informational):
`b01f517680458786ac5750d89ce31b5f02604d09a2ead9daa7adcd668116d0a6`

Required rejection: the `grant` records are not in strict ascending
`(grantee_control_role, privilege)` order. The first record `(3, SELECT)` is
followed by the smaller `(2, SELECT)` record, so this body is noncanonical and
must reject before any accepted L2 value is returned.
